description_full: Fortuna Mining Corp. engages in the precious and base metal mining and related activities in Argentina, Côte d'Ivoire, Mexico, Peru, and Senegal. The company operates through Mansfield, Sango, and Bateas segments. It operates the Lindero gold mine and the Séguéla gold mine, as well as the Caylloma silver, lead, and zinc mine. The company also holds Bambadji advanced gold exploration project located in Senegal. The company was formerly known as Fortuna Silver Mines Inc. and changed its name to Fortuna Mining Corp. in June 2024. Fortuna Mining Corp. was incorporated in 1990 and is based in Vancouver, Canada.

financial_summary: Fortuna Mining Corp. is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $2.8B market cap on $947M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +12% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 34%.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin -0.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.4%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 3.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

Trade policy and tariff whiplash — materials producers are first-order casualties of protectionist swings, and margin gets squeezed from both input and output pricing.

It captures 3.29x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.04 across 219 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 40% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 31% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 58% and a beta of 1.03, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 2.26 vs 5y 1.07), so read it loosely.
About $51.7M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 56% in the 2020 crash, 53% in the 2022 bear market and 90% in 2008.
val: The stock trades only 9% below its blended-model fair value of $10.59, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 42%), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Basic Materials peers: P/E 10.1 vs 16.5 and EV/EBITDA 3.3 vs 8.5 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 52% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an EBIT/EV of 16.3% (vs the 8% bar).
The Street target $14.50 on average, 51% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 8% falls short of the cost of capital of 9.9%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.29).
ROE of 19% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.4x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 24pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $554.0M.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 11.6% over 3 years and 27.7% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 37%).

own: Insiders hold little stock (0.6%), and institutions hold 80%.
Shareholder yield is a modest 0.4% (0.4% in buybacks).

people: The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
